title: The old quarter
description: An isolated historic quarter sits within a wider valley. Use its small building scale and the contrast between settlement and countryside.
developer_note: Keep the camera fixed when changing settlement size. Alter lot count and footprint instead of enlarging houses.
sound_note: In the café court, bring cup clinks and footsteps close. Muffle them as focus moves behind the corner.

title: The arcades
description: Arcaded frontages make a dense but bounded market town. Recessed walkways and small courts distinguish shop lots.
developer_note: Tag porticoes as sheltered frontage. Keep supports and passable openings on consistent anchors.
sound_note: Move under an arch to soften the rainfall. Let individual drops from the eaves strike the paving just beyond it.

title: Weavers' lanes
description: Timber gables and artisan workshops diversify the silhouette. Roof heights and materials vary within a coherent old district.
developer_note: Select related timber patterns per district and enforce a roof-height variation budget.
sound_note: Give one workshop a loom shuttle. Let its dry wooden tap carry a short distance along the wet lane.

title: The terraced town
description: A compact town uses retaining walls, stair links and irregular terraces. Terrain relief is gentler than the later L studies.
developer_note: Keep house baselines level while foundation steps absorb changes in ground height.
sound_note: Follow a flight of steps. Shift the footfall to wet stone, then soften it when the landing slips behind a wall.

title: Market crossroads
description: A covered market forms a local center where narrow routes meet. Housing loosens around it.
developer_note: Reserve the market as a bounded lot before streets and facade decoration are resolved.
sound_note: Let rain patter on the market roof. Bring up the quieter murmur underneath as the listener enters the stall.

title: School street
description: The school and playground form a recognizable civic pair within mixed residential streets.
developer_note: Reserve the school footprint and play lot together, then keep their entrances linked to the street graph.
sound_note: Ring the school bell once on focus. Carry a softer version into the next street while the rain continues.

title: The garden town
description: Detached homes, greenhouses and gardens take more frontage. A short commercial group anchors the center.
developer_note: Garden and greenhouse lots provide low built density without simply removing all street activity.
sound_note: At the park gate, bring out drips collecting in the leaves. Let the café voices recede behind the hedge.

title: The orchard village
description: An orchard separates two small groups of houses. Productive landscape becomes part of the settlement.
developer_note: Place orchard rows in agricultural parcels. Break their rhythm near gates and paths.
sound_note: Move from shelter into the orchard. Trade drips from the eaves for the softer patter of rain on fallen leaves.

title: Along the farm lane
description: A rural ribbon of houses and barns sits among open fields. The inn and its neighbors provide one gathering place.
developer_note: Keep the lane narrow and continuous. Use barns and fences as distinct rural lot types.
sound_note: Give the farm lane a gravel footfall. A gate opening adds a brief timber creak against the steady rain.

title: The hamlet square
description: A few buildings enclose an intimate well court. Fields and meadow dominate the wider view.
developer_note: Stop spawning houses once the hamlet count is met. Use the remaining space for landscape.
sound_note: Let a cup set down outside the inn be audible in the little square. Out in the meadow, leave room for rain and wind.

title: Continuous old town
description: Historic blocks fill the available view through many small buildings and layered streets.
developer_note: Increase building count and depth bands while preserving the established small facade scale.
sound_note: Try the changing shelter of arcades, enclosed courts and narrow lanes as the listener moves through the old town.

title: Dense town with garden districts
description: Dense historic streets contain garden districts and civic openings. This is a sprawl reference; T01-T05 govern a true taper.
developer_note: Do not infer a density gradient from this image. Use the later transition family for thinning streets.
sound_note: Let café activity thin out toward the garden streets, where drops from hedges and individual footsteps become more distinct.

title: Historic streets with modern infill
description: Modern infill appears within historic blocks. Balconies, flat roofs and broad civic windows add a second architectural language.
developer_note: Modern modules need separate roof, opening and balcony rules, with shared watercolor treatment.
sound_note: Compare rainfall on glass canopies, timber cladding and the stone thresholds of older shops.

title: Old quarter and postwar neighborhoods
description: A historic center connects to postwar walk-up apartments, villas and newer homes.
developer_note: Use district-level architectural weights to form neighborhoods rather than random style changes per house.
sound_note: Give the schoolyard, apartment court and café square separate local ambiences, with softer sound from the streets behind.

title: Contemporary town around an old core
description: Contemporary low-rise buildings surround a recognizable old core. Modern roofs and larger openings remain softly painted.
developer_note: Balance modern and historic massing. Civic anchors should remain identifiable at the distant camera.
sound_note: A sheltered community-center entrance and the open old square offer two different listening spaces within the same neighborhood.

title: Town across the foothills
description: Dense blocks on the left loosen into terraces, garden streets and a handful of homes at the woodland edge.
developer_note: Inspect the decrease in frontage attachment and increase in open lot width through every depth band. Retain a connected route to the last house.
